name: Aghanashini

sink.name: Near Aghanashini village, Kumta taluk
sink.location: Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka, Arabian Sea

significance: estuarine fisheries and salt-tolerant paddy farming
did_you_know: The Aghanashini is one of the very few undammed, free-flowing rivers left in peninsular India, its entire course running through forest and farmland without a major dam.
Its wide estuary supports thousands of fishing and farming families, including cultivation of Kagga, a distinctive salt-tolerant rice grown in tidal 'Gazni' fields.
Its name is shared, confusingly, with an older historical alias of the separate Zuari river in Goa — the two are unrelated rivers roughly 150 km apart.
